name: Humanitarian Data Exchange
tagline: Find, share and use humanitarian data all in one place
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: OCHA (UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs)
dependency_risks: Dependent on OCHA funding and institutional support

academic_citations.citation: Meier, P. (2015). Digital Humanitarians: How Big Data is Changing the Face of Humanitarian Response. CRC Press.

policy_outcomes: Improved data standardization in humanitarian sector
Increased transparency in crisis response operations
published_performance_metrics: Data sharing volume increased 300% since 2014; 1000+ organizations registered
documented_limitations: Data quality varies by contributing organization
Limited coverage in some regions with limited internet connectivity
failure_modes: Data gaps in conflict zones with limited access
Inconsistent data formats from different contributors
curation_criteria: Data must be relevant to humanitarian response, include metadata, and follow HDX data standards
contributor_governance: Open contribution model with OCHA review and validation process
disparity_tracking: Tracks geographic coverage gaps and identifies underrepresented regions

government_partnerships.partner: OCHA (UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs)

ai_involvement: Limited - basic search and recommendation features
political_relevance_summary: Humanitarian Data Exchange addresses the civic problem of making civic data accessible and actionable. It has documented policy impact.

movement_building_utility.notes: Serves as an information resource: Find, share and use humanitarian data all in one place.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase enables replication. already deployed internationally across multiple jurisdictions.
